title: Likelihood and a prior
summary: What MLE maximizes, and when MAP becomes ridge.

choices.text: Maximum likelihood maximizes p(data | θ); for linear regression with Gaussian noise it is least squares. MAP also multiplies by a prior, and a zero-mean Gaussian prior on the weights gives ridge regression.

Maximum likelihood maximizes p(data | θ); for linear regression with Gaussian noise it is least squares. MAP also multiplies by a prior, and a zero-mean Gaussian prior on the weights gives the lasso and its sparse solutions.
MAP maximizes p(θ | data). With any prior it returns exactly the maximum-likelihood answer once there are more rows than weights, so the prior only matters on tiny datasets.
Maximum likelihood maximizes p(θ | data) directly, while MAP maximizes p(data | θ) and adds a prior term; a Gaussian prior on the weights makes MAP ordinary least squares.
